newsitem.title: JAPAN: Russia's Primakov in Japan over islands dispute.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Primakov in Japan over islands dispute.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov arrived in Tokyo on Thursday to hold the latest round of talks over an islands dispute with Japan, but neither side expected any real development in the drawn-out row.

On Friday, Primakov will hold two sessions with Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda and a short meeting with Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, foreign ministry officials said. He leaves for China on Sunday.
Both Russia and Japan are not ready for any concession on the dispute over the islands, located northeast of Japan's northernmost main island of Hokkaido, diplomatic sources said.

They said Japan cannot be seen giving in to Russia on the question of sovereignty over what it calls the Northern Territories and Russia calls the Southern Kuriles because it could affect Tokyo's other disputes on islands.

Japan has recently found itself embroiled in heated disputes with China over what it calls the Senkaku Islands in the East China Sea, known as Diaoyus in Chinese, and with South Korea over Takeshima in the Sea of Japan, called Tokdo by Seoul.
The row over the islands seized by the Soviet Red Army in the closing days of World War Two has prevented the formal conclusion of a peace treaty between the two countries.
Until 1993 when President Boris Yeltsin came to Tokyo, Russia did not even agree that a dispute had existed.
But Yeltsin cannot afford to make any move now over Russian territory anywhere out of fear of a nationalistic backlash in his country, diplomatic sources said.

The biggest fear for Japan is that Primakov may formally propose a joint development scheme of the islands -- Etorofu, Shikotan, Kunashiri and the Habomai group -- after setting aside the question of sovereignty.
"We are ready to listen to such a proposal, so long as it does not affect our fundamental claim over the islands," Foreign Ministry spokesman Hiroshi Hashimoto said.
Britain and Argentina have embarked on such a scheme over the Falkland Islands in the South Atlantic, called Malvinas by Buenos Aires, which the two countries fought a war over in 1982.

Barring any real advance over the territorial dispute, Primakov and Ikeda were expected to sit down and work out a programme for improving overall ties, including increasing exchange of visa-free visits, promoting business ties between Japan and Russia's Far East region, and moving ahead on fishing ties between the two countries.
Other issues on the agenda include a trip to Tokyo by Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov and bilateral trade talks, both scheduled for next year.
